newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CA Czech unit says approved for mortgage bonds.
newsitem.headline: CA Czech unit says approved for mortgage bonds.

text.p: The Czech unit of Austria's Creditanstalt Bankverein said on Tuesday it received Czech National Bank (CNB) approval to issue mortgage-backed bonds.

"Banka Creditanstalt a.s. received from the Czech National Bank a licence to issue mortgage-backed bonds. That means that Creditanstalt can begin to grant to its clients classical mortgage loans," the bank said in a statement.
Creditanstalt said it would begin to offer mortgage credit in first-quarter 1997. The first mortgage-backed bond issue was also expected some time in 1997.

It said it would begin offering long-term financing of real estate to a selected group of private clients, making use of the state support programme that will subsidise up to four percentage points of the interest payments of the credit.

"In the area of granting credit to legal entities, Creditanstalt will prefer companies interested in investing into real estate intended for enterprises and housing and companies engaged in building activities in the (Czech Republic", it said.
It said the bank would offer mortgage credit with fixed and variable interest rates pegged to a fixed indicator. The statement did not say what would be the basis for such an indicator.

Creditanstalt's Czech unit, with total basic capital of 1.7 billion crowns and a balance sheet total at the end of 1995 of 21.9 billion crowns, is 100-percent owned by the Austrian parent and has been been active on the Czech market since 1991.
It has eight branches operating in major Czech cities with a ninth branch planned to open by the end of the year in the second-largest city, Brno.
